o_XVt5rdpFY.title: The Secrets of Learning a New Language

cues.text: I love learning foreign languages.
cues.en: I love learning foreign languages.
cues.zh: 我熱愛學習外語。

cues.text: In fact, I love it so much that I like to learn a new language every two years,
cues.en: In fact, I love it so much that I like to learn a new language every two years,
cues.zh: 其實我愛到每兩年就學一種新語言，

cues.text: currently working on my eighth one.
cues.en: currently working on my eighth one.
cues.zh: 目前我在學第八種語言。

cues.text: When people find that out about me, they always ask me,
cues.en: When people find that out about me, they always ask me,
cues.zh: 如果有人發現這件事， 他們都會問我，

cues.text: "How do you do that? What's your secret?"
cues.en: "How do you do that? What's your secret?"
cues.zh: 「你是怎麼辦到的？秘訣是什麼？」

cues.text: And to be honest, for many years, my answer would be,
cues.en: And to be honest, for many years, my answer would be,
cues.zh: 老實說，多年來我的答案大多是：

cues.text: "I don't know. I simply love learning languages."
cues.en: "I don't know. I simply love learning languages."
cues.zh: 「不知道耶！我就是愛學語言。」

cues.text: But people were never happy with that answer.
cues.en: But people were never happy with that answer.
cues.zh: 但大家對這個答案都不滿意。

cues.text: They wanted to know why they are spending years trying to learn even one language,
cues.en: They wanted to know why they are spending years trying to learn even one language,
cues.zh: 他們想知道，為何自己費時多年， 而且只學一種語言，

cues.text: never achieving fluency,
cues.en: never achieving fluency,
cues.zh: 還是無法說得流利，

cues.text: and here I come, learning one language after another.
cues.en: and here I come, learning one language after another.
cues.zh: 而我卻能一個語言接著一個語言學。

cues.text: They wanted to know the secret of polyglots,
cues.en: They wanted to know the secret of polyglots,
cues.zh: 他們想知道語言達人的秘訣，

cues.text: people who speak a lot of languages.
cues.en: people who speak a lot of languages.
cues.zh: 精通多種語言者的秘訣。

cues.text: And that made me wonder, too,
cues.en: And that made me wonder, too,
cues.zh: 這也勾起了我的好奇心，

cues.text: how do actually other polyglots do it?
cues.en: how do actually other polyglots do it?
cues.zh: 其他語言達人是怎麼辦到的？

cues.text: What do we have in common?
cues.en: What do we have in common?
cues.zh: 我們有什麼共通點？

cues.text: And what is it that enables us
cues.en: And what is it that enables us
cues.zh: 是什麼因素讓我們

cues.text: to learn languages so much faster than other people?
cues.en: to learn languages so much faster than other people?
cues.zh: 比其他人學語言的速度還快得多？

cues.text: I decided to meet other people like me and find that out.
cues.en: I decided to meet other people like me and find that out.
cues.zh: 我決定和其他像我這樣的人 見面來找出答案。

cues.text: The best place to meet a lot of polyglots
cues.en: The best place to meet a lot of polyglots
cues.zh: 要碰到很多語言達人的最佳地點

cues.text: is an event where hundreds of language lovers
cues.en: is an event where hundreds of language lovers
cues.zh: 就在幾百位語言愛好者參加的聚會，

cues.text: meet in one place to practice their languages.
cues.en: meet in one place to practice their languages.
cues.zh: 大家在同一個地方 練習自己在學的語言。

cues.text: There are several such polyglot events organized all around the world,
cues.en: There are several such polyglot events organized all around the world,
cues.zh: 世界各地都有一些這種 辦給語言達人參加的活動，

cues.text: and so I decided to go there
cues.en: and so I decided to go there
cues.zh: 所以我決定去那

cues.text: and ask polyglots about the methods that they use.
cues.en: and ask polyglots about the methods that they use.
cues.zh: 問問語言達人他們用了什麼方法。

cues.text: And so I met Benny from Ireland,
cues.en: And so I met Benny from Ireland,
cues.zh: 我碰到從愛爾蘭來的白尼，

cues.text: who told me that his method is to start speaking from day one.
cues.en: who told me that his method is to start speaking from day one.
cues.zh: 他告訴我，他的方法是 從第一天就開始說。

cues.text: He learns a few phrases from a travel phrasebook
cues.en: He learns a few phrases from a travel phrasebook
cues.zh: 他先從旅遊書籍學幾個詞，

cues.text: and goes to meet native speakers
cues.en: and goes to meet native speakers
cues.zh: 然後去和當地人碰面，

cues.text: and starts having conversations with them right away.
cues.en: and starts having conversations with them right away.
cues.zh: 馬上和他們對話。

cues.text: He doesn't mind making even 200 mistakes a day,
cues.en: He doesn't mind making even 200 mistakes a day,
cues.zh: 他不介意每天犯多達兩百個錯誤，

cues.text: because that's how he learns, based on the feedback.
cues.en: because that's how he learns, based on the feedback.
cues.zh: 因為他就是這樣 從別人給的回饋學習。

cues.text: And the best thing is, he doesn't even need to travel a lot today,
cues.en: And the best thing is, he doesn't even need to travel a lot today,
cues.zh: 最棒的是，現在 他根本不用到處旅行，

cues.text: because you can easily have conversations with native speakers
cues.en: because you can easily have conversations with native speakers
cues.zh: 因為你可以輕易和當地人 在你舒適的客廳交談，

cues.text: from the comfort of your living room, using websites.
cues.en: from the comfort of your living room, using websites.
cues.zh: 只要有網路就行。

cues.text: I also met Lucas from Brazil
cues.en: I also met Lucas from Brazil
cues.zh: 我也碰到巴西來的盧卡斯，

cues.text: who had a really interesting method to learn Russian.
cues.en: who had a really interesting method to learn Russian.
cues.zh: 他學俄語的方法超有趣。

cues.text: He simply added a hundred random Russian speakers on Skype as friends,
cues.en: He simply added a hundred random Russian speakers on Skype as friends,
cues.zh: 他在 Skype 上任意 加一百個說俄語的人好友，

cues.text: and then he opened a chat window with one of them
cues.en: and then he opened a chat window with one of them
cues.zh: 然後開啟其中一個人的對話視窗，

cues.text: and wrote "Hi" in Russian.
cues.en: and wrote "Hi" in Russian.
cues.zh: 用俄語寫「嗨」。

cues.text: And the person replied, "Hi, how are you?"
cues.en: And the person replied, "Hi, how are you?"
cues.zh: 這個人回：「嗨，你好嗎？」

cues.text: Lucas copied this and put it into a text window with another person,
cues.en: Lucas copied this and put it into a text window with another person,
cues.zh: 盧卡斯把這句話覆製貼到 另一個人的對話視窗，

cues.text: and the person replied, "I'm fine, thank you, and how are you?"
cues.en: and the person replied, "I'm fine, thank you, and how are you?"
cues.zh: 這個人回： 「我很好，謝謝，你呢？」

cues.text: Lucas copied this back to the first person,
cues.en: Lucas copied this back to the first person,
cues.zh: 他再把這句話覆製，貼給第一個人，

cues.text: and in this way, he had two strangers have a conversation with each other
cues.en: and in this way, he had two strangers have a conversation with each other
cues.zh: 透過這個方法， 他讓兩個陌生人交談，

cues.text: without knowing about it.
cues.en: without knowing about it.
cues.zh: 而且他們自己根本不知道。

cues.text: (Laughter)
cues.en: (Laughter)
cues.zh: （笑聲）

cues.text: And soon he would start typing himself,
cues.en: And soon he would start typing himself,
cues.zh: 不久後他就可以開始自己打字，

cues.text: because he had so many of these conversations
cues.en: because he had so many of these conversations
cues.zh: 因為有過這麼多對話之後，

cues.text: that he figured out how the Russian conversation usually starts.
cues.en: that he figured out how the Russian conversation usually starts.
cues.zh: 他就知道要怎麼開始用俄語交談。

cues.text: What an ingenious method, right?
cues.en: What an ingenious method, right?
cues.zh: 很天才的方法，對吧？

cues.text: And then I met polyglots who always start by imitating sounds of the language,
cues.en: And then I met polyglots who always start by imitating sounds of the language,
cues.zh: 後來我碰到一個語言達人， 他都會從模仿一個語言的聲音開始；

cues.text: and others who always learn the 500 most frequent words of the language,
cues.en: and others who always learn the 500 most frequent words of the language,
cues.zh: 有一部分的人會先學 最常用的五百個單字；

cues.text: and yet others who always start by reading about the grammar.
cues.en: and yet others who always start by reading about the grammar.
cues.zh: 還有一些人會先學文法。

cues.text: If I asked a hundred different polyglots,
cues.en: If I asked a hundred different polyglots,
cues.zh: 如果我問一百個語言達人，

cues.text: I heard a hundred different approaches to learning languages.
cues.en: I heard a hundred different approaches to learning languages.
cues.zh: 會聽到一百種不同的語言學習法。

cues.text: Everybody seems to have a unique way they learn a language,
cues.en: Everybody seems to have a unique way they learn a language,
cues.zh: 每個人都有自己 獨特的方式學習語言，

cues.text: and yet we all come to the same result of speaking several languages fluently.
cues.en: and yet we all come to the same result of speaking several languages fluently.
cues.zh: 最後大家都能流利說多種語言。

cues.text: And as I was listening to these polyglots telling me about their methods,
cues.en: And as I was listening to these polyglots telling me about their methods,
cues.zh: 聽著其他達人說他們的方法時，

cues.text: it suddenly dawned on me:
cues.en: it suddenly dawned on me:
cues.zh: 我突然明白：

cues.text: the one thing we all have in common
cues.en: the one thing we all have in common
cues.zh: 我們的共通點

cues.en: is that we simply found ways to enjoy the language-learning process.

cues.text: All of these polyglots were talking about language learning

cues.zh: 所有達人在談語言學習的時候

cues.text: as if it was great fun.
cues.en: as if it was great fun.
cues.zh: 都像是學語言超有趣。

cues.text: You should have seen their faces
cues.en: You should have seen their faces
cues.zh: 可惜你們沒看到他們

cues.text: when they were showing me their colorful grammar charts
cues.en: when they were showing me their colorful grammar charts
cues.zh: 給我看他們做的彩色文法表、

cues.zh: 每個人都採用不同方法，

cues.text: but they always make sure it's something that they personally enjoy.
cues.en: but they always make sure it's something that they personally enjoy.

cues.text: I realized that this is actually how I learn languages myself.
cues.en: I realized that this is actually how I learn languages myself.
cues.zh: 我理解到其實這也是 我自己學語言的方法。

cues.text: When I was learning Spanish, I was bored with the text in the textbook.
cues.en: When I was learning Spanish, I was bored with the text in the textbook.
cues.zh: 我學西班牙語的時候， 覺得課本上的文章很無聊。

cues.text: I mean, who wants to read about Jose

cues.zh: 我的意思是，誰會想讀

cues.text: asking about the directions to the train station. Right?

cues.zh: 何西問去火車站要怎麼走？

cues.text: I wanted to read "Harry Potter" instead,
cues.en: I wanted to read "Harry Potter" instead,
cues.zh: 我反而想先讀《哈利波特》，

cues.text: because that was my favorite book as a child,
cues.en: because that was my favorite book as a child,
cues.zh: 因為那是我小時候最愛的書，

cues.text: and I have read it many times.
cues.en: and I have read it many times.
cues.zh: 我看過很多次了。

cues.text: So I got the Spanish translation of "Harry Potter" and started reading,
cues.en: So I got the Spanish translation of "Harry Potter" and started reading,
cues.zh: 所以我找到這本書的西班牙語譯本，

cues.text: and sure enough, I didn't understand almost anything at the beginning,

cues.text: I can watch it in any language. I love it so much.

cues.text: seriously, the dialogue started to make sense.

cues.en: You’re in what’s called a knowledge gap.

cues.en: There’s more information you need in order to understand the facts

cues.en: Gilbert has just presented to you.

cues.en: He and his coworkers have been researching something called impact bias,

cues.text: which is the tendency for our experience simulators to work badly—

cues.text: to make us believe different experiences are more different
cues.en: to make us believe different experiences are more different
cues.zh: 讓我們以為不同的人生經歷，

cues.text: than they actually are.
cues.en: than they actually are.
cues.zh: 帶來的感受差異比實際上大得多。

cues.text: By putting a name on it, impact bias,
cues.en: By putting a name on it, impact bias,
cues.zh: 當這個現象有了「影響偏誤」這個名稱，

cues.text: the mystery of the information we’re struggling to make sense of
cues.en: the mystery of the information we’re struggling to make sense of
cues.zh: 原本讓我們困惑不解的結果， 也開始顯得合理。

cues.text: starts to become more believable.
cues.en: starts to become more believable.
cues.zh: 我們的好奇心也比剛才更加強烈。

cues.en: Our curiosity is now burning more brightly than before.
cues.zh: 我們的好奇心也比剛才更加強烈。

cues.text: In fact, they really are, from field studies to laboratory studies,

cues.zh: 事實上，從實地研究到實驗室研究，

cues.text: have far less impact, less intensity, and much less duration

cues.text: than people expect them to have.

cues.text: suggests that if it happened over three months ago, with only a few exceptions,

cues.zh: 研究發現，除了一些例外，

cues.text: it has no impact whatsoever on your happiness.
cues.en: it has no impact whatsoever on your happiness.

cues.en: Because happiness can be synthesized.

cues.text: Sir Thomas Brown wrote in 1642, “I am the happiest man alive.

cues.zh: 我比阿基里斯更加無堅不摧， 命運找不到可以攻擊我的地方。」

cues.zh: 在舉出幾個合成幸福 實際運作的例子後，

cues.en: He goes on to show how you can live a wiser, happier life
cues.zh: 他進一步說明：只要記得 「合成幸福」確實存在，

cues.en: if you remember synthetic happiness exists.

cues.en: and raised roughly $82 million in government revenue.
cues.zh: 也為政府帶來大約 8,200 萬美元的稅收。

cues.text: However, it also increased the average price of washing machines by $86,
cues.en: However, it also increased the average price of washing machines by $86,
cues.zh: 然而，這項政策也讓洗衣機的 平均價格提高了 86 美元，

cues.text: costing consumers roughly $1.5 billion.
cues.en: costing consumers roughly $1.5 billion.
cues.zh: 讓消費者多支出約 15 億美元。

cues.text: This means consumers paid roughly $817,000 to create each of those jobs.
cues.en: This means consumers paid roughly $817,000 to create each of those jobs.
cues.zh: 換句話說，為了創造這些工作機會，

cues.text: In other cases, the jobs tariffs create come at the cost of existing jobs.
cues.en: In other cases, the jobs tariffs create come at the cost of existing jobs.
cues.zh: 有些情況則是，關稅創造了新的工作， 卻也讓原有的工作消失。

cues.text: In 2002, the Bush administration imposed tariffs as high as 30%
cues.en: In 2002, the Bush administration imposed tariffs as high as 30%
cues.zh: 2002 年，布希政府對進口鋼鐵 課徵最高達 30% 的關稅。

cues.text: on imported steel.
cues.en: on imported steel.
cues.zh: 當時，美國鋼鐵業的就業人數 已經衰退了幾十年，

cues.text: Employment in US steel production had been decaying for decades,
cues.en: Employment in US steel production had been decaying for decades,
cues.zh: 當時，美國鋼鐵業的就業人數 已經衰退了幾十年，

cues.text: so by making foreign steel more expensive,
cues.en: so by making foreign steel more expensive,
cues.zh: 因此政府希望藉由 提高外國鋼鐵的價格，

cues.text: the tariff sought to create new jobs for US steel manufacturers.
cues.en: the tariff sought to create new jobs for US steel manufacturers.
cues.zh: 為美國鋼鐵製造商創造新的工作機會。

cues.text: Initially, the policy did slow down job loss.
cues.en: Initially, the policy did slow down job loss.
cues.zh: 起初，這項政策確實 減緩了失業的速度。

cues.text: But since US steel still cost more than pre-tariff foreign steel,
cues.en: But since US steel still cost more than pre-tariff foreign steel,
cues.zh: 然而，由於美國鋼鐵的價格 仍高於課徵關稅前的進口鋼材，

cues.text: domestic industries that used this material had to increase their prices.
cues.en: domestic industries that used this material had to increase their prices.
cues.zh: 使用鋼鐵作為原料的國內產業 也只好提高產品價格。

cues.text: This made their products less competitive internationally,
cues.en: This made their products less competitive internationally,
cues.zh: 這讓它們在國際市場上的競爭力下降，

cues.text: where foreign manufacturers were still using cheap steel.
cues.en: where foreign manufacturers were still using cheap steel.
cues.zh: 因為外國製造商仍然使用便宜的鋼材。

cues.text: Within a year of enacting the tariff,
cues.en: Within a year of enacting the tariff,
cues.zh: 一年之內，美國在鋼鐵相關產業 流失的工作機會，

cues.text: the US lost far more jobs in steel-related industries
cues.en: the US lost far more jobs in steel-related industries
cues.zh: 一年之內，美國在鋼鐵相關產業 流失的工作機會，

cues.text: than they gained in steel-producing industries.
cues.en: than they gained in steel-producing industries.
cues.zh: 就遠遠超過鋼鐵生產業 所新增的工作機會。

cues.text: Clearly, how other countries respond to tariffs
cues.en: Clearly, how other countries respond to tariffs
cues.zh: 顯然，其他國家如何回應關稅，

cues.text: is another big part of the ripple effect these policies have.
cues.en: is another big part of the ripple effect these policies have.
cues.zh: 也是這些政策所引發 連鎖效應中的重要一環。

cues.text: One clear example comes from 2018,
cues.en: One clear example comes from 2018,
cues.zh: 2018 年就有一個很清楚的例子。

cues.text: when the US attempted to address its trade deficit with China
cues.en: when the US attempted to address its trade deficit with China
cues.zh: 當時，美國試圖透過 對中國商品課徵關稅，

cues.text: by taxing Chinese goods.
cues.en: by taxing Chinese goods.
cues.zh: 來改善美中之間的貿易逆差。

cues.text: While these tariffs protected domestic businesses
cues.en: While these tariffs protected domestic businesses
cues.zh: 這些關稅雖然保護了美國國內企業，

cues.text: and raised government revenue,
cues.en: and raised government revenue,
cues.zh: 也增加了政府收入，

cues.text: they also set off a trade war.
cues.en: they also set off a trade war.
cues.zh: 卻同時引發一場貿易戰。

cues.text: China retaliated by raising tariffs on US exporters,
cues.en: China retaliated by raising tariffs on US exporters,
cues.zh: 中國提高美國商品的 進口關稅作為報復，

cues.text: including farmers relying on Chinese markets for soybean sales.
cues.en: including farmers relying on Chinese markets for soybean sales.
cues.zh: 其中包括美國農民仰賴 中國銷售的黃豆。

cues.text: In the end, this led to higher prices for US consumers
cues.en: In the end, this led to higher prices for US consumers
cues.zh: 最後，這場貿易戰導致美國消費者 承受更高的物價，

cues.text: and a slight drop in America's GDP.
cues.en: and a slight drop in America's GDP.
cues.zh: 也讓美國的國內生產毛額 （GDP）小幅下降。

cues.text: Trade wars aren’t new.
cues.en: Trade wars aren’t new.
cues.zh: 貿易戰並不是新鮮事。

cues.text: And even in the 18th and early 19th centuries,
cues.en: And even in the 18th and early 19th centuries,
cues.zh: 在 18 世紀和 19 世紀初，

cues.text: when certain tariffs did help struggling industries find their domestic footing,
cues.en: when certain tariffs did help struggling industries find their domestic footing,
cues.zh: 即使某些關稅政策確實有助 陷入困境的產業在國內站穩腳步，

cues.text: they were mostly used to raise government funds.
cues.en: they were mostly used to raise government funds.
cues.zh: 關稅最主要的用途仍是增加政府收入。

cues.text: But over the last 200 years,
cues.en: But over the last 200 years,
cues.zh: 但過去 200 年來，

cues.text: our global economy has become far more interdependent.
cues.en: our global economy has become far more interdependent.
cues.zh: 全球經濟的相互依賴程度 已經大幅提高。

cues.text: Today, there are more manufacturing components
cues.en: Today, there are more manufacturing components
cues.zh: 如今，各國進口的 製造零元件之多，更甚以往，

cues.text: being imported than ever before,
cues.en: being imported than ever before,
cues.zh: 如今，各國進口的 製造零元件之多，更甚以往，

cues.text: many of which are used to make a wide variety of consumer goods.
cues.en: many of which are used to make a wide variety of consumer goods.
cues.zh: 而其中許多零元件又會被用來 製造各式各樣的消費商品。

cues.text: This complexity means that even a seemingly simple tariff
cues.en: This complexity means that even a seemingly simple tariff
cues.zh: 這種複雜的經濟關係意味著，

cues.text: can trigger a global chain reaction,
cues.en: can trigger a global chain reaction,
cues.zh: 即使看似簡單的一項關稅， 也可能引發全球性的連鎖反應，

cues.text: creating more consequences than anyone can plan for.
cues.en: creating more consequences than anyone can plan for.
cues.zh: 造成遠超乎預期的後果。

JOs-q7rXqdk.title: 4 Ways to Tell a Great Story

cues.text: Your first job as a speaker is to build a trusting human bond
cues.en: Your first job as a speaker is to build a trusting human bond
cues.zh: 演講者首先要做的，

cues.text: with your audience.
cues.en: with your audience.
cues.zh: 和聽眾建立連結的 一個好方法，就是說故事。

cues.text: One excellent way to connect to an audience is to tell a story.
cues.en: One excellent way to connect to an audience is to tell a story.
cues.zh: 和聽眾建立連結的 一個好方法，就是說故事。

cues.text: Stories helped make us who we are.
cues.en: Stories helped make us who we are.
cues.zh: 故事塑造了我們， 讓我們成為今天的樣子。

cues.text: Really — evidence left behind from our ancient ancestors
cues.en: Really — evidence left behind from our ancient ancestors
cues.zh: 真的，我們的遠古祖先 留下的證據顯示，

cues.text: suggests that the human mind developed alongside human storytelling.
cues.en: suggests that the human mind developed alongside human storytelling.
cues.zh: 人類心智的發展， 是隨著說故事的能力一起進步的。

cues.text: Fire created a new magnet for bonding.
cues.en: Fire created a new magnet for bonding.
cues.zh: 火堆提供人們情感連結的凝聚力。

cues.text: Its warmth and flickering light drew people together after dark.
cues.en: Its warmth and flickering light drew people together after dark.
cues.zh: 天黑之後，火的溫暖與搖曳的光芒， 將人們聚集在一起。

cues.text: This seems to have happened in every ancient culture
cues.en: This seems to have happened in every ancient culture
cues.zh: 過去三十萬年來，

cues.text: over the last 300,000 years.
cues.en: over the last 300,000 years.
cues.zh: 這樣的情景似乎出現在 每一個古老文化中。

cues.text: And what did our ancestors do with this time together?
cues.en: And what did our ancestors do with this time together?
cues.zh: 那麼，我們的祖先會利用 這段團聚時光做什麼事呢？

cues.text: In many cultures,
cues.en: In many cultures,
cues.zh: 在許多文化裡，

cues.text: one type of communal activity became very important: storytelling.
cues.en: one type of communal activity became very important: storytelling.
cues.zh: 有一項共同活動顯得特別重要， 那就是說故事。

cues.text: Stories brought people from faraway places to the fireside.
cues.en: Stories brought people from faraway places to the fireside.
cues.zh: 故事把來自遠方的人吸引到火堆旁。

cues.text: Stories about people who were alive and people who were dead,
cues.en: Stories about people who were alive and people who were dead,
cues.zh: 故事描述活著的人，也講述死去的人；

cues.text: nearby and in distant lands.
cues.en: nearby and in distant lands.
cues.zh: 故事裡有附近的人， 也有生活在遙遠土地上的人。

cues.text: Stories sparked laughter, tension, and amazement.
cues.en: Stories sparked laughter, tension, and amazement.
cues.zh: 故事讓人笑、讓人屏息，也讓人驚嘆。

cues.text: Stories also played an important role in helping expand people’s ability
cues.en: Stories also played an important role in helping expand people’s ability
cues.zh: 故事另一個重要功能是

cues.text: to imagine and to dream, and to understand the minds of others.
cues.en: to imagine and to dream, and to understand the minds of others.
cues.zh: 幫助人們拓展想像力與夢想，

cues.text: Storytellers became important people within a community,
cues.en: Storytellers became important people within a community,
cues.zh: 說書人逐漸成為社群中的重要人物，

cues.text: and their listeners took information from the stories
cues.en: and their listeners took information from the stories
cues.zh: 而聽故事的人也會 從故事中得到一些訊息，

cues.text: that changed how they behaved in the world.
cues.en: that changed how they behaved in the world.
cues.zh: 進而影響他們看待世界和行事的方式。

cues.text: It's not just that we all love hearing stories.
cues.en: It's not just that we all love hearing stories.
cues.zh: 這不只是因為每個人都喜歡聽故事，

cues.text: Stories probably helped shape how our minds share and receive information.
cues.en: Stories probably helped shape how our minds share and receive information.
cues.zh: 而是故事很可能早已形塑了 我們分享與接收資訊的方式。

cues.text: So it's no surprise that many of the best talks are built around a story.
cues.en: So it's no surprise that many of the best talks are built around a story.
cues.zh: 難怪，許多精彩的演講 都是以故事為核心。

cues.text: The most basic way of breaking down a story is this:
cues.en: The most basic way of breaking down a story is this:
cues.zh: 最基本的故事結構，可以這樣拆解：

cues.text: a character with a goal meets an unexpected obstacle.
cues.en: a character with a goal meets an unexpected obstacle.
cues.zh: 一個角色，有追求的目標， 遇上了意料之外的障礙。

cues.text: She tries to overcome that obstacle, which builds to a peak in the action.
cues.en: She tries to overcome that obstacle, which builds to a peak in the action.
cues.zh: 她試著克服這個障礙， 情節因此逐漸推向高潮。

cues.text: Finally, there’s some kind of resolution to the conflict.
cues.en: Finally, there’s some kind of resolution to the conflict.
cues.zh: 最後，衝突以某種方式獲得解決。

cues.text: When it comes to sharing a story from the stage,
cues.en: When it comes to sharing a story from the stage,
cues.zh: 如果你要在臺上分享一個故事，

cues.text: remember four key things:
cues.en: remember four key things:
cues.zh: 請記住四件重要的事。

cues.text: 1. Base the story around a character your audience can empathize with.
cues.en: 1. Base the story around a character your audience can empathize with.
cues.zh: 第一，讓故事圍繞著一個 聽眾能夠產生共鳴的角色。

cues.text: 2. Build tension,
cues.en: 2. Build tension,
cues.zh: 第二，營造緊張感，

cues.text: either through curiosity, relationship with other characters, or actual danger.
cues.en: either through curiosity, relationship with other characters, or actual danger.
cues.zh: 可以勾起好奇心、發展人物關係， 或加入真正的危險。

cues.text: 3. Offer the right level of detail.
cues.en: 3. Offer the right level of detail.
cues.zh: 第三，提供適量的細節。

cues.text: If there's not enough, the story won't come to life.
cues.en: If there's not enough, the story won't come to life.
cues.zh: 如果細節不夠，故事就無法鮮活起來；

cues.text: If there's too much, it will get bogged down.
cues.en: If there's too much, it will get bogged down.
cues.zh: 但如果細節太多，故事又會拖泥帶水。

cues.text: And, 4. End with a satisfying conclusion, whether it’s funny, moving, or surprising.
cues.en: And, 4. End with a satisfying conclusion, whether it’s funny, moving, or surprising.
cues.zh: 第四，用令人滿意的結尾收束故事， 不論結尾好笑、感人，還是出人意料。

cues.text: Some great talks are built around a single story.
cues.en: Some great talks are built around a single story.
cues.zh: 有些精彩的演講， 就圍繞著一個故事展開。

cues.text: This can be really helpful for a speaker.
cues.en: This can be really helpful for a speaker.
cues.zh: 對演講者來說，這是很有幫助的，

cues.text: The throughline is simply the plot of the story.
cues.en: The throughline is simply the plot of the story.
cues.zh: 因為故事的情節本身， 就能成為整場演講的主線。

cues.text: If the story is about you, it can even create empathy in the audience.
cues.en: If the story is about you, it can even create empathy in the audience.
cues.zh: 如果故事講的是你自己的經歷， 還能讓聽眾對你產生同理心。

cues.text: If your journey is exciting and easy to follow,
cues.en: If your journey is exciting and easy to follow,
cues.zh: 如果你的故事精彩，情節又清楚易懂，

cues.text: this type of talk can work really well.
cues.en: this type of talk can work really well.
cues.zh: 這種演講方式就能發揮很好的效果。

cues.text: But there's a trap here too.
cues.en: But there's a trap here too.
cues.zh: 但這裡也有一個陷阱。

cues.text: Remember, the goal is to give.
cues.en: Remember, the goal is to give.
cues.zh: 別忘了，演講的目的 是要帶給聽眾一些東西。

cues.text: Personal stories may entertain or interest an audience,
cues.en: Personal stories may entertain or interest an audience,
cues.zh: 個人故事也許能娛樂或吸引聽眾，

cues.text: or make the speaker feel really good about themselves,
cues.en: or make the speaker feel really good about themselves,
cues.zh: 或者讓演講者自我感覺良好，

cues.text: but they don’t necessarily give the audience
cues.en: but they don’t necessarily give the audience
cues.zh: 但不一定能讓聽眾得到有價值的東西，

cues.text: something they can walk away with;
cues.en: something they can walk away with;
cues.zh: 例如新的觀點、實用的資訊、 看事情的脈絡，或一點希望。

cues.text: a new way of understanding things, actionable information, context, hope.
cues.en: a new way of understanding things, actionable information, context, hope.
cues.zh: 例如新的觀點、實用的資訊、 看事情的脈絡，或一點希望。

cues.text: And that’s a real shame.
cues.en: And that’s a real shame.
cues.zh: 如果沒有這些，那就真的很可惜。

cues.text: The key is to link together the important moments of your story
cues.en: The key is to link together the important moments of your story
cues.zh: 關鍵在於，要把你故事中 那些重要的時刻串聯起來，

cues.text: in a way that can be meaningful to someone else.
cues.en: in a way that can be meaningful to someone else.
cues.zh: 讓它們對其他人也具有意義。

cues.text: Otherwise, it may sound like you're just rambling
cues.en: Otherwise, it may sound like you're just rambling
cues.zh: 否則，聽起來就可能像是在東拉西扯，

cues.text: or speaking for the sake of hearing yourself talk.
cues.en: or speaking for the sake of hearing yourself talk.
cues.zh: 只是為了自己想說而說。

cues.text: But, if the journey reveals something powerful you have learned,
cues.en: But, if the journey reveals something powerful you have learned,
cues.zh: 然而，如果你想藉由這個旅程 揭示某個你學到的重要道理，

cues.text: and if each step in your journey is revealed with humility and honesty
cues.en: and if each step in your journey is revealed with humility and honesty
cues.zh: 而你又能以謙遜、誠實 和坦然面對脆弱的態度，

cues.text: and vulnerability,
cues.en: and vulnerability,
cues.zh: 呈現旅程中的每一步，

cues.text: it is a journey we will gladly take with you.
cues.en: it is a journey we will gladly take with you.
cues.zh: 那麼我們就會很樂意 和你一起走完這段旅程。

cues.text: There is one other piece that is absolutely essential
cues.en: There is one other piece that is absolutely essential
cues.zh: 如果你打算說自己的故事，

cues.text: if you’re going to tell your own story:
cues.en: if you’re going to tell your own story:
cues.zh: 還有一點非常關鍵：

cues.text: it has to be true.
cues.en: it has to be true.
cues.zh: 這必須是個真實的故事。

cues.text: This may seem obvious,
cues.en: This may seem obvious,
cues.zh: 這聽起來也許很理所當然，

cues.text: but sometimes speakers are tempted to exaggerate
cues.en: but sometimes speakers are tempted to exaggerate
cues.zh: 但有時候，講者會忍不住誇大其詞，

cues.text: or even make a story up entirely.
cues.en: or even make a story up entirely.
cues.zh: 甚至乾脆捏造整個故事。

cues.text: Stories can have such a big impact that some speakers
cues.en: Stories can have such a big impact that some speakers
cues.zh: 故事的影響力有時很大，

cues.text: are tempted to bend the truth.
cues.en: are tempted to bend the truth.
cues.zh: 因此有些演講者會忍不住 加油添醋，甚至扭曲事實。

cues.text: But even small exaggerations can quickly destroy your reputation.
cues.en: But even small exaggerations can quickly destroy your reputation.
cues.zh: 但即使只是些微的誇大， 也可能很快毀掉你的信譽。

cues.text: It's not worth the risk.
cues.en: It's not worth the risk.
cues.zh: 不值得冒這種風險。

cues.text: When you combine a truthful story with a desire to benefit others,
cues.en: When you combine a truthful story with a desire to benefit others,
cues.zh: 當你說的故事是真實的， 目的只是想給別人幫助，

cues.text: you can give your listeners an extraordinary gift.
cues.en: you can give your listeners an extraordinary gift.
cues.zh: 你送給聽眾的就是一份非凡的禮物。

cues.text: A story can affect people deeply.
cues.en: A story can affect people deeply.
cues.zh: 故事能夠深深觸動人心。

cues.text: Use it, and you can greatly increase your connection with an audience.
cues.en: Use it, and you can greatly increase your connection with an audience.
cues.zh: 善用故事，就能讓你 和聽眾建立更深的連結。

cues.text: But please, let it mean something.
cues.en: But please, let it mean something.
cues.zh: 但請記得，你的故事要有意義。

cues.text: To coincide with the 1964 Tokyo Olympics,
cues.en: To coincide with the 1964 Tokyo Olympics,
cues.zh: 為配合 1964 年東京奧運會，

cues.text: Japan launched the world’s first high-speed train, the Shinkansen.
cues.en: Japan launched the world’s first high-speed train, the Shinkansen.
cues.zh: 日本推出了全球第一條高速鐵路——

cues.zh: 我們能做些什麼，

cues.text: to prevent those cultures from taking hold before they harden.
cues.en: to prevent those cultures from taking hold before they harden.
cues.zh: 在這些文化成形、僵化之前， 就阻止它們蔓延。

cues.text: And what I've learned is this.
cues.en: And what I've learned is this.
cues.zh: 以下是我所學到的。

cues.text: First, bullying is not conflict.
cues.en: First, bullying is not conflict.
cues.zh: 首先，霸凌不是衝突。

cues.text: It's not a debate,
cues.en: It's not a debate,
cues.zh: 它不是辯論，

cues.text: it's not criticism,
cues.en: it's not criticism,
cues.zh: 不是批評，

cues.text: it's not humor that you're too sensitive to take well.
cues.en: it's not humor that you're too sensitive to take well.
cues.zh: 也不是你太敏感、 才承受不了的玩笑。

cues.text: It is a deliberately targeted,
cues.en: It is a deliberately targeted,
cues.zh: 霸凌是由多人刻意針對一個人，

cues.text: serial, escalating pattern of attacks
cues.en: serial, escalating pattern of attacks
cues.zh: 一次又一次發動愈演愈烈的攻擊，

cues.text: carried out by multiple people,
cues.en: carried out by multiple people,
cues.zh: 一次又一次發動愈演愈烈的攻擊，

cues.text: and it's intended to destroy a person's reputation
cues.en: and it's intended to destroy a person's reputation
cues.zh: 目的就是摧毀那個人的聲譽，

cues.text: and their ability to contribute.
cues.en: and their ability to contribute.
cues.zh: 以及他為群體做出貢獻的能力。

cues.text: It unfolds in predictable stages.
cues.en: It unfolds in predictable stages.
cues.zh: 霸凌依循可預測的階段一步步發展。

cues.text: And it usually ends with someone being completely silenced
cues.en: And it usually ends with someone being completely silenced
cues.zh: 而結局通常就是讓某個人徹底噤聲，

cues.text: or disappearing completely.
cues.en: or disappearing completely.
cues.zh: 或者徹底消失。

cues.text: This is really important.
cues.en: This is really important.
cues.zh: 這一點非常重要。

cues.text: Bullies are rare.
cues.en: Bullies are rare.
cues.zh: 霸凌者是少數。

cues.text: They're rare.
cues.en: They're rare.
cues.zh: 他們是少數。

cues.text: Most of us are not bullies.
cues.en: Most of us are not bullies.
cues.zh: 我們大多數人都不是霸凌者。

cues.text: Bullies share one thing:
cues.en: Bullies share one thing:
cues.zh: 霸凌者有一個共同點：

cues.text: a worldview.
cues.en: a worldview.
cues.zh: 他們有一套特定的世界觀。

cues.text: In their worldview,
cues.en: In their worldview,
cues.zh: 在他們的世界裡，

cues.text: the world is hostile,
cues.en: the world is hostile,
cues.zh: 世界充滿敵意，

cues.text: people are fundamentally bad,
cues.en: people are fundamentally bad,
cues.zh: 人性本惡，

cues.text: everything of value is scarce,
cues.en: everything of value is scarce,
cues.zh: 有價值的東西都是稀缺的，

cues.text: it’s all zero-sum.
cues.en: it’s all zero-sum.
cues.zh: 樣樣都是零和遊戲。

cues.text: Your achievement is their loss.
cues.en: Your achievement is their loss.
cues.zh: 你的成就，就是他們的損失。

cues.text: They have an insatiable need for recognition and status and dominance,
cues.en: They have an insatiable need for recognition and status and dominance,
cues.zh: 他們對認可、地位和主導優勢 有著永遠無法滿足的渴望，

cues.text: and they prove their dominance
cues.en: and they prove their dominance
cues.zh: 而他們證明自己具有主導地位的方式，

cues.text: by publicly demonstrating that they can force a target,
cues.en: by publicly demonstrating that they can force a target,
cues.zh: 就是公開展示自己能迫使一個目標——

cues.text: a valuable target, to fully submit.
cues.en: a valuable target, to fully submit.
cues.zh: 有價值的目標——完全屈服。

cues.text: That's what bullying is.
cues.en: That's what bullying is.
cues.zh: 這就是霸凌的本質。

cues.text: Bullying has been on the rise among adults for the last 15 years.
cues.en: Bullying has been on the rise among adults for the last 15 years.
cues.zh: 過去 15 年來， 成人間的霸凌現象與日俱增。

cues.text: Digital platforms make bullying faster, easier, louder.
cues.en: Digital platforms make bullying faster, easier, louder.
cues.zh: 數位平臺讓霸凌變得更快、 更容易，聲勢也更浩大。

cues.text: And the bullies' lies last forever now.
cues.en: And the bullies' lies last forever now.
cues.zh: 如今，霸凌者散播的謊言 甚至可以永遠留存。

cues.text: So ...
cues.en: So ...
cues.zh: 那麼……

cues.text: What do we do?
cues.en: What do we do?
cues.zh: 我們該怎麼辦？

cues.text: The first thing to understand is that bullies need us.
cues.en: The first thing to understand is that bullies need us.
cues.zh: 首先，我們必須明白， 霸凌者需要我們。

cues.text: Bullies need an audience.
cues.en: Bullies need an audience.
cues.zh: 霸凌者需要觀眾。

cues.text: They need people to carry out their agenda.
cues.en: They need people to carry out their agenda.
cues.zh: 他們需要有人替他們達成目的。

cues.text: When we just watch and remain silent,
cues.en: When we just watch and remain silent,
cues.zh: 當我們袖手旁觀、保持沉默時，

cues.text: we're what I call passive bystanders.
cues.en: we're what I call passive bystanders.
cues.zh: 我們就成為所謂的「被動旁觀者」。

cues.text: When we join in and amplify and share an attack,
cues.en: When we join in and amplify and share an attack,
cues.zh: 當我們加入其中， 助紂為虐、轉傳攻擊時，

cues.text: we're what I call accessory bullies.
cues.en: we're what I call accessory bullies.
cues.zh: 我們就成了「霸凌的幫兇」。

cues.text: But if we refuse our participation,
cues.en: But if we refuse our participation,
cues.zh: 但如果我們拒絕參與，

cues.text: a lone bully is impotent.
cues.en: a lone bully is impotent.
cues.zh: 孤立的霸凌者就無能為力。

cues.text: Without us, a bully is impotent.
cues.en: Without us, a bully is impotent.
cues.zh: 沒有我們，霸凌者就無能為力。

cues.text: (Applause)
cues.en: (Applause)
cues.zh: （掌聲）

cues.text: Second, we need to learn to spot the opening.
cues.en: Second, we need to learn to spot the opening.
cues.zh: 第二，我們要學會察覺介入的時機。

cues.text: When we get in early,
cues.en: When we get in early,
cues.zh: 如果我們及早介入，

cues.text: we can totally derail this.
cues.en: we can totally derail this.
cues.zh: 就能徹底阻撓霸凌的程序。

cues.text: It starts with what I call a “bully test.”
cues.en: It starts with what I call a “bully test.”
cues.zh: 事情往往從我所謂的 「霸凌測試」開始。

cues.text: The bully tests the audience to see if they can get away
cues.en: The bully tests the audience to see if they can get away
cues.zh: 霸凌者會先試探旁觀者，

cues.text: with bullying that person.
cues.en: with bullying that person.
cues.zh: 可能是在專業場合 說出非常不恰當的話，

cues.text: It might be a really inappropriate comment in a professional setting,
cues.en: It might be a really inappropriate comment in a professional setting,
cues.zh: 可能是在專業場合 說出非常不恰當的話，

cues.text: or it might be an accusation
cues.en: or it might be an accusation
cues.zh: 也可能是對某人提出 足以摧毀其聲譽的指控，

cues.text: against someone that’s reputation-destroying,
cues.en: against someone that’s reputation-destroying,
cues.zh: 卻沒有任何證據支援。

cues.text: but not backed by evidence.
cues.en: but not backed by evidence.
cues.zh: 卻沒有任何證據支援。

cues.text: When we hear those things and we stay silent or we laugh,
cues.en: When we hear those things and we stay silent or we laugh,
cues.zh: 當我們聽到這些話， 卻保持沉默，甚至跟著笑，

cues.text: we're just saying to the bully, "Go forward."
cues.en: we're just saying to the bully, "Go forward."
cues.zh: 我們其實就是在 對霸凌者說：「繼續。」

cues.text: And that's when they launch their attack.
cues.en: And that's when they launch their attack.
cues.zh: 而這時，他們就會發動攻擊。

cues.text: We also need to practice social bravery.
cues.en: We also need to practice social bravery.
cues.zh: 我們還需要培養所謂的「社會勇氣」。

cues.text: These small risks that we take to defend each other,
cues.en: These small risks that we take to defend each other,
cues.zh: 也就是在人際相處時， 願意冒一點小小的風險，

cues.text: to support each other interpersonally.
cues.en: to support each other interpersonally.
cues.zh: 為彼此挺身而出、支援彼此。

cues.text: And social bravery is risky.
cues.en: And social bravery is risky.
cues.zh: 而社會勇氣確實伴隨風險。

cues.text: So we need to distribute the risk across people.
cues.en: So we need to distribute the risk across people.
cues.zh: 所以，我們需要讓更多人 共同承擔這個風險。

cues.text: We need to do it together.
cues.en: We need to do it together.
cues.zh: 我們需要一起做。

cues.text: It is so much easier for two people to do it
cues.en: It is so much easier for two people to do it
cues.zh: 兩個人一起做， 要比一個人單獨做容易得多。

cues.text: than for one person to do it.
cues.en: than for one person to do it.
cues.zh: 當一名旁觀者以明確、 顯著的方式挺身而出，

cues.text: When one bystander steps in, in a way that’s noticeable,
cues.en: When one bystander steps in, in a way that’s noticeable,
cues.zh: 當一名旁觀者以明確、 顯著的方式挺身而出，

cues.text: others step in.
cues.en: others step in.
cues.zh: 其他人也會跟著站出來。

cues.text: And we know from research on changing social conventions
cues.en: And we know from research on changing social conventions
cues.zh: 從改變社會規範的研究中，我們知道，

cues.text: that when about 25 percent of people step in,
cues.en: that when about 25 percent of people step in,
cues.zh: 當大約 25% 的人願意挺身而出，

cues.text: they can flip a social norm completely.
cues.en: they can flip a social norm completely.
cues.zh: 就能徹底扭轉一項社會規範。

cues.text: Bullying is not a personal problem.
cues.en: Bullying is not a personal problem.
cues.zh: 霸凌不是個人的問題，

cues.text: It's a collective problem.
cues.en: It's a collective problem.
cues.zh: 而是集體的問題。

cues.text: And we can fix it.
cues.en: And we can fix it.
cues.zh: 我們可以解決。

cues.text: So after eight years of writing this book,
cues.en: So after eight years of writing this book,
cues.zh: 花了八年寫完這本書後，

cues.text: I turned it in a few months ago.
cues.en: I turned it in a few months ago.
cues.zh: 我幾個月前把稿子交了出去。

cues.text: Right after that,
cues.en: Right after that,
cues.zh: 緊接著，

cues.text: I traveled to Greeley, Colorado,
cues.en: I traveled to Greeley, Colorado,
cues.zh: 我前往科羅拉多州的格里利，

cues.text: a small city in the High Plains
cues.en: a small city in the High Plains
cues.zh: 一座位於高地平原地區的小城市。

cues.text: that was raw,
cues.en: that was raw,
cues.zh: 當時那裡氣氛緊繃、

cues.text: politically divided, on edge.
cues.en: politically divided, on edge.
cues.zh: 政治立場分裂，劍拔弩張。

cues.text: I could feel the vigilance in the air when I looked at them.
cues.en: I could feel the vigilance in the air when I looked at them.
cues.zh: 我看著聽眾，就能感受到 現場瀰漫著戒備的氣氛。

cues.text: I spoke about personal power and trust,
cues.en: I spoke about personal power and trust,
cues.zh: 我談到個人力量與信任，

cues.text: and at the end the moderator said her last question to me was this.
cues.en: and at the end the moderator said her last question to me was this.
cues.zh: 最後，主持人問我一個問題。

cues.text: She said,
cues.en: She said,
cues.zh: 她說：

cues.text: "Is there one piece of leadership advice
cues.en: "Is there one piece of leadership advice
cues.zh: 「能不能給我們一項你從未分享過的

cues.text: that you haven't really shared?"
cues.en: that you haven't really shared?"
cues.zh: 有關領導力的建議？」

cues.text: And I said, “Yeah.
cues.en: And I said, “Yeah.
cues.zh: 我說：「好的。

cues.text: We'll never win by bullying the bullies.
cues.en: We'll never win by bullying the bullies.
cues.zh: 我們永遠不可能靠霸凌霸凌者來獲勝。

cues.text: We cannot validate their worldview.
cues.en: We cannot validate their worldview.
cues.zh: 我們不能認可他們的世界觀是對的。

cues.text: As soon as we tell them that the world has to be brutal,
cues.en: As soon as we tell them that the world has to be brutal,
cues.zh: 因為一旦我們告訴他們， 這個世界本來就必須如此殘酷，

cues.text: they say, ’See?
cues.en: they say, ’See?
cues.zh: 他們就會說：『你看吧？

cues.text: That’s why I have to behave this way.“’
cues.en: That’s why I have to behave this way.“’
cues.zh: 所以我才得這樣做。』」

cues.text: I told them you don’t have to show how much you can hate
cues.en: I told them you don’t have to show how much you can hate
cues.zh: 我告訴他們，你不需要展現 自己有多恨一個人，

cues.text: to prove how much you care, or to prove that you belong.
cues.en: to prove how much you care, or to prove that you belong.
cues.zh: 才能證明你有多在乎，

cues.text: And I looked out and I saw their shoulders relax.
cues.en: And I looked out and I saw their shoulders relax.
cues.zh: 我看向臺下，看見聽眾的肩膀 放鬆了下來。

cues.text: I saw a flicker of hope in their faces.
cues.en: I saw a flicker of hope in their faces.
cues.zh: 我看見他們臉上閃過一絲希望。

cues.text: I felt them collectively exhale.
cues.en: I felt them collectively exhale.
cues.zh: 我感覺到他們一起鬆了一口氣。

cues.text: And the next day a woman wrote to me.
cues.en: And the next day a woman wrote to me.
cues.zh: 第二天，一位女士寫信給我。

cues.text: And she said, "I was at your talk.
cues.en: And she said, "I was at your talk.
cues.zh: 她說：「我當時在現場聽你的演講。

cues.text: And I noticed something interesting as I left the venue.
cues.en: And I noticed something interesting as I left the venue.
cues.zh: 離開會場時，我注意到 一件很有意思的事。

cues.text: The crowd was unusually cheerful and courteous.
cues.en: The crowd was unusually cheerful and courteous.
cues.zh: 群眾異常地愉快，也特別有禮貌。

cues.text: Several drive aisles wove together toward the exits,
cues.en: Several drive aisles wove together toward the exits,
cues.zh: 好幾條車道交織著通往出口，

cues.text: and everyone was alternating and letting each other in.
cues.en: and everyone was alternating and letting each other in.
cues.zh: 而每個人都輪流讓對方先走。

cues.text: No one was saying with their actions
cues.en: No one was saying with their actions
cues.zh: 沒有人用行動表現出 「我比別人重要」。

cues.text: that they were more important than another person.
cues.en: that they were more important than another person.
cues.zh: 沒有人用行動表現出 「我比別人重要」。

cues.text: I just wanted to share the observation
cues.en: I just wanted to share the observation
cues.zh: 我只是想告訴你，我觀察到：

cues.text: that you made an immediate, positive and tangible difference."
cues.en: that you made an immediate, positive and tangible difference."
cues.zh: 你的演講帶來了立即、 正面而具體的改變。」

cues.text: (Applause)
cues.en: (Applause)
cues.zh: （掌聲）

cues.text: We want to be neighbors again.
cues.en: We want to be neighbors again.
cues.zh: 我們想重新成為鄰居。

cues.text: We want to go to our kids' friends' birthday parties
cues.en: We want to go to our kids' friends' birthday parties
cues.zh: 我們想去參加孩子朋友的生日派對，

cues.text: and not worry about an explosion.
cues.en: and not worry about an explosion.
cues.zh: 而不用擔心現場突然爆發衝突。

cues.text: We don't want to have to show how much we hate
cues.en: We don't want to have to show how much we hate
cues.zh: 我們不想再需要展現自己有多恨，

cues.text: to prove how much we care.
cues.en: to prove how much we care.
cues.zh: 才能證明自己有多在乎。

cues.text: Bullies' power is borrowed power.
cues.en: Bullies' power is borrowed power.
cues.zh: 霸凌者的力量，是借來的力量。

cues.text: And we can refuse to give it to them.
cues.en: And we can refuse to give it to them.
cues.zh: 而我們可以拒絕把這份力量借給他們。

cues.text: We all have access to personal power, and with that personal power,
cues.en: We all have access to personal power, and with that personal power,
cues.zh: 我們每個人都擁有 運用個人力量的能力，

cues.text: we can commit small acts of social bravery,
cues.en: we can commit small acts of social bravery,
cues.zh: 而憑藉這份個人力量，我們可以 做出一個個小小的社會勇敢行動，

cues.text: supporting each other,
cues.en: supporting each other,
cues.zh: 彼此支援，

cues.text: challenging bullies.
cues.en: challenging bullies.
cues.zh: 向霸凌者提出挑戰。

cues.text: So I invite you please, to join me.
cues.en: So I invite you please, to join me.
cues.zh: 我想邀請你，請加入我。

cues.text: Let's find that collective power
cues.en: Let's find that collective power
cues.zh: 讓我們找到這股集體的力量，

cues.text: and turn bullying around.
cues.en: and turn bullying around.
cues.zh: 扭轉霸凌的局面。

cues.text: And one more thing.
cues.en: And one more thing.
cues.zh: 還有一件事。

cues.text: (Cheers and applause)
cues.en: (Cheers and applause)
cues.zh: （歡呼與掌聲）

cues.text: Thank you.
cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 謝謝你們。

cues.text: Thank you so much.
cues.en: Thank you so much.
cues.zh: 非常謝謝。

cues.text: (Applause)
cues.en: (Applause)
cues.zh: （掌聲）

cues.en: it can spark transformation in our workplaces

cues.text: and in our families.

cues.text: And I learned this lesson the way that I learned most things,
cues.en: And I learned this lesson the way that I learned most things,

SjvS20YqUJ4.title: How to Negotiate Your Salary Effectively

cues.en: Negotiating your salary is one of the most important professional skills.
cues.zh: 談判薪資是最關鍵的職場專業技能之一。

cues.en: Most people feel uncomfortable asking for more money during an interview.
cues.zh: 大多數人在面試時對於要求更多薪資感到不自在。

cues.en: However, research shows that those who negotiate earn significantly more over their lifetime.
cues.zh: 然而研究顯示，主動談判的人終身收入明顯更高。

cues.en: Start by doing thorough market research to understand your true market value.
cues.zh: 首先進行徹底的市場研究，了解自己真正的市場價值。

cues.en: Focus on the value and measurable impact you bring to the company.
cues.zh: 將焦點放在你能為公司帶來的價值與具體成果上。

cues.en: Frame your request around shared goals and long-term success.
cues.zh: 將你的要求圍繞在共同目標與長期成功之上。

cues.en: Always be prepared with alternatives such as remote work or extra vacation days.
cues.zh: 隨時準備好遠端工作或額外年假等彈性替代方案。

cues.en: Confidence and preparation make all the difference in any negotiation.
cues.zh: 自信與充分準備是在任何談判中勝出的關鍵。

cues.en: Inflation is the general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.
cues.zh: 通貨膨脹是指物價普遍上漲，貨幣購買力下降。

cues.en: When money supply grows faster than the economic output, inflation usually follows.
cues.zh: 當貨幣供給增長速度快於經濟產出時，通膨通常隨之而來。

cues.en: Central banks use interest rates to cool down an overheating economy.
cues.zh: 各國央行透過調整利率來給過熱的經濟降溫。

cues.en: Moderate inflation of around two percent is actually considered healthy for growth.
cues.zh: 適度維持約百分之二的溫和通膨其實被視為有益於成長。

cues.en: Understanding inflation helps you make smarter investments and protect your savings.
cues.zh: 了解通貨膨脹有助於做出更聰明的投資並守護存款。

EbsU0reInPI.title: How Berkshire Hathaway Became an Empire

cues.en: Warren Buffett transformed a struggling textile company into a global conglomerate.
cues.zh: 華倫·巴菲特將一家陷入困境的紡織公司轉型為跨國商業帝國。

cues.en: His core philosophy centers on value investing and long-term compounding.
cues.zh: 他的核心哲學圍繞在價值投資與長期的複利力量。

cues.en: Buy companies with durable competitive advantages and hold them forever.
cues.zh: 收購具備持久競爭優勢的好公司，並長期持有。

cues.en: Patience and emotional discipline are the true secrets to financial independence.
cues.zh: 耐心與情緒紀律才是達成財務自由的真正秘訣。

jYWF64Um7pw.title: Mastering the Art of Pitching to Investors

cues.en: A great pitch starts with a clear problem and a massive market opportunity.
cues.zh: 出色的提案始於一個清晰的痛點與龐大的市場契機。

cues.en: Investors want to know why your team is uniquely qualified to solve this problem.
cues.zh: 投資人想知道為何你的團隊具備獨一無二的資格來解決這個難題。

cues.en: Keep your presentation concise, data-driven, and emotionally compelling.
cues.zh: 保持簡報簡明扼要、以數據為支撐，且具備感染力。

cues.en: Traction speaks louder than any slide deck or projections.
cues.zh: 真實的用戶增長數據勝過任何精美的簡報與預測。

jTW777ENc3c.title: The Power of Compound Interest Explained

cues.en: Compound interest is interest calculated on the initial principal and accumulated interest.
cues.zh: 複利是以最初本金加上過去累積利息一起計算的利息。

cues.en: Albert Einstein reportedly called it the eighth wonder of the world.
cues.zh: 據傳愛因斯坦稱之為世界第八大奇蹟。

cues.en: The earlier you start investing, the more time your money has to grow.
cues.zh: 你越早開始投資，你的資金就有越多時間成長滾雪球。

cues.en: Even small monthly contributions can turn into substantial wealth over decades.
cues.zh: 即使每個月只投入小額資金，數十年後也能變成可觀財富。

cues.en: Being busy is not the same thing as being productive.
cues.zh: 瞎忙碌並不等於真正有高生產力。

cues.en: Focus on the twenty percent of activities that generate eighty percent of your results.
cues.zh: 專注於能創造百分之八十成果的那百分之二十關鍵工作。

cues.en: Eliminate distractions and protect deep work time every morning.
cues.zh: 消除干擾，每天早晨保護好專注進行深度工作的時間。

cues.en: Learn to say no to requests that do not align with your core mission.
cues.zh: 學會對那些不符合你核心目標的瑣碎請求說不。

8cF442d-EdQ.title: How Remote Work Changed Global Commerce

cues.en: The transition to remote work is the largest workplace experiment in history.
cues.zh: 轉向遠端工作是人類歷史上規模最大的職場實驗。

cues.en: Companies now hire top global talent regardless of physical location.
cues.zh: 企業如今可以在不受地理位置限制的情況下聘用全球頂尖人才。

cues.en: Asynchronous communication requires better documentation and clear trust.
cues.zh: 非同步溝通需要更扎實的文件記錄與彼此清晰的信任。

Pydut1BMlBw.title: How to Build a Startup with Zero Capital

cues.en: You do not need millions in funding to test a business idea.
cues.zh: 你不需要百萬資金也能驗證一個商業構想。

cues.en: Find your first three paying customers before you build any product.
cues.zh: 在你動手打造產品前，先找到前三位願意付費的顧客。

cues.en: Customer feedback is the only compass that truly matters for founders.
cues.zh: 客戶的真實反饋才是創業者唯一重要的指針。

cues.en: Apple built the most profitable consumer hardware ecosystem in modern history.
cues.zh: 蘋果打造了現代歷史上獲利最豐厚的消費性硬體生態系。

cues.en: Seamless integration between devices creates tremendous switching costs for users.
cues.zh: 裝置間的無縫整合為用戶帶來了巨大的轉換成本。

cues.en: Services like iCloud and Apple Music provide predictable recurring revenue.
cues.zh: iCloud 與 Apple Music 等服務提供了穩定可預期的經常性收入。

cues.en: Luxury is not about utility; it is fundamentally about emotional signaling.
cues.zh: 奢華無關實用功能，其本質是情感與社會身分的信號傳遞。

cues.en: Artificial scarcity creates an irresistible aura of desirability and prestige.
cues.zh: 人為製造的稀缺性營造了令人難以抗拒的渴望與尊榮感。

cues.en: Heritage and storytelling transform raw materials into cultural mythology.
cues.zh: 歷史傳承與品牌敘事將普通的原材料轉化為文化神話。

-JNjsOX0N0c.title: Shadowing Technique: The Ultimate Fluency Hack

cues.en: Shadowing is speaking along with a native audio track with almost zero delay.
cues.zh: 跟讀法就是在幾乎零延遲的情況下跟著母語音檔一起開口朗讀。

cues.en: It forces your vocal muscles to adapt to the speed and rhythm of natural speech.
cues.zh: 它強迫你的發聲肌肉群適應自然對話的速度與節奏。

cues.en: Start with short sentences and gradually increase length as your confidence grows.
cues.zh: 從簡短的句子開始，隨著信心建立再逐漸增加句子長度。

YAsDeXcYyTg.title: Overcome the Fear of Speaking English

cues.en: Perfectionism is the biggest obstacle to speaking a foreign language.
cues.zh: 完美主義是開口說外語時最大的心理障礙。

cues.en: Native speakers care about understanding your message, not your grammar mistakes.
cues.zh: 母語人士在乎的是理解你的意思，而不是計較你的文法小錯誤。

cues.en: Start speaking to yourself out loud for five minutes every single day.
cues.zh: 從每天對著自己大聲開口說英文五分鐘開始練習。

cues.en: Celebrate small victories and remember that making mistakes is how learning happens.
cues.zh: 慶祝每一個小進步，並記住犯錯正是學習發生的途徑。

LDkvRFCm8No.title: The Real Difference Between British and American English

cues.en: British and American English are two branches of the same beautiful language.
cues.zh: 英式與美式英語是同一個美麗語言的兩大分支。

cues.en: Notice how Americans pronounce the 'r' sound while Brits often drop it.
cues.zh: 注意美式發音會清晰捲起 'r' 音，而英式則常常弱化或省略。

cues.en: Vocabulary differences like 'boot' versus 'trunk' can lead to funny misunderstandings.
cues.zh: 像 'boot' 和 'trunk'（後車廂）的詞彙差異常引發有趣的誤會。

topBLaz4zgk.title: How to Ask Smart Questions in Conversations

cues.en: Great conversationalists ask open-ended questions that spark genuine storytelling.
cues.zh: 優秀的對話者善於提出開放式問題，能激發對方真誠分享故事。

cues.en: Avoid questions that can be answered with a simple yes or no.
cues.zh: 避免提出那種只能用簡短的是或不是回答的問題。

cues.en: Ask 'How did that feel?' rather than just 'What happened?'
cues.zh: 多問問「當時感受如何？」而不僅僅是「發生了什麼事？」。

cues.en: The schwa is the most common sound in the English language.
cues.zh: 中央弱母音 /ə/ 是英語中最常見的發音。

cues.en: It appears in unstressed syllables of words like 'banana' and 'computer'.
cues.zh: 它出現在像 'banana' 和 'computer' 的非重音節當中。

cues.en: Relax your jaw and let the sound out effortlessly without tension.
cues.zh: 放鬆下巴，毫不費力且毫無緊繃感地發出這個短音。

hZc2l3Pm2Sk.title: How to Deliver an Unforgettable Toast or Speech

cues.en: A memorable speech has a clear beginning, an honest story, and a warm call to action.
cues.zh: 令人難忘的演講具備清晰的開場、真誠的故事與溫暖的呼籲。

cues.en: Make eye contact with different members of your audience throughout the room.
cues.zh: 在演說過程中與台下各個角落的聽眾進行眼神交流。

cues.en: Pauses can be more powerful than words when used at dramatic moments.
cues.zh: 在關鍵轉折點適當停頓，往往比滔滔不絕更有力量。

hglYQqRGbng.title: Mastering English Phrasal Verbs in Context

cues.en: Phrasal verbs combine a verb with a preposition to create entirely new meanings.
cues.zh: 動詞片語將動詞與介系詞結合，產生截然不同的全新含義。

cues.en: Learning them in complete stories makes remembering them intuitive and long-lasting.
cues.zh: 在完整故事語境中學習，能讓記憶更直觀且更深刻持久。

cues.en: Practice using them in your own conversations to solidify your active vocabulary.
cues.zh: 在日常對話中主動使用它們，將被動字彙轉化為流暢主動語料。

cues.en: A vaccine introduces an antigen that teaches the immune system to recognize pathogens.
cues.zh: 疫苗引入抗原，教導人體免疫系統學會識別病原體。

cues.en: White blood cells produce custom antibodies designed to neutralize the threat.
cues.zh: 白血球產生專屬抗體，專門用來中和外來威脅。

cues.en: Memory cells remain in the body, ready to respond rapidly to future infections.
cues.zh: 記憶細胞會在體內長期存留，準備在未來遭遇感染時迅速反應。

cues.en: Throughout history, humans have wondered about the hidden meaning of dreams.
cues.zh: 縱觀歷史，人類始終對夢境中隱藏的深層含義感到好奇。

cues.en: During REM sleep, your brain is almost as active as when you are fully awake.
cues.zh: 在快速動眼期（REM）睡眠中，大腦的活躍程度幾乎與清醒時無異。

cues.en: Some scientists believe dreaming helps consolidate memories and solve creative problems.
cues.zh: 有些科學家認為做夢有助於鞏固記憶並激發創意思考。

7yDmGnA8Hw0.title: Can You Solve the Elevator Riddle?

cues.text: Welcome back to our exploration of Can You Solve the Elevator Riddle?.
cues.zh: 歡迎回到我們對「Can You Solve the Elevator Riddle?」的深度探索。

cues.text: Today, we are examining the core principles behind this fascinating topic.
cues.zh: 今天，我們將深入剖析這個迷人主題背後的核心原理。

cues.text: Many experts agree that understanding this mechanism changes how we see the world.
cues.zh: 許多專家都認同，理解這項機制將徹底改變我們看待世界的方式。

cues.text: Let's break down the essential details step by step.
cues.zh: 讓我們一步步拆解其中的關鍵細節。

cues.text: Notice how each component interacts seamlessly with the surrounding environment.
cues.zh: 請注意每個組成部分是如何與周遭環境無縫互動的。

cues.text: By applying this knowledge, we can achieve far greater clarity and confidence.
cues.zh: 透過應用這項知識，我們能夠獲得更清晰的理解與充沛的自信。

cues.text: Thank you for watching, and keep practicing your English every single day!
cues.zh: 感謝收看，記得每天都要持續練習英文喔！

p7HKvqRI_Bo.title: How Does the Stock Market Work?

cues.en: A company sells shares to the public to raise funds for expanding its operations.
cues.zh: 公司向大眾出售股份，以籌募擴大業務營運所需的資金。

cues.en: When many people want to buy a particular stock, its price goes up.
cues.zh: 當許多人都想買進某支特定股票時，其價格就會水漲船高。

cues.en: Investors earn money through dividend distributions and rising stock values.
cues.zh: 投資人透過股利分紅與股票增值來賺取資本回報。

A2m4wzDH05Q.title: What If the Earth Stopped Spinning?

cues.en: Earth spins at roughly one thousand miles per hour at the equator.
cues.zh: 地球在赤道處的自轉時速大約高達一千英里。

cues.en: If it suddenly stopped, inertia would send everything hurtling eastward at tremendous speeds.
cues.zh: 如果它突然停下，慣性會將地表萬物以驚人速度拋向東方。

cues.en: Oceans would migrate toward the poles, completely redrawing all global coastlines.
cues.zh: 各大洋的海水會向兩極湧去，徹底重繪全球的所有海岸線。

cues.en: A hotel with infinitely many rooms is completely full, yet a new guest arrives.
cues.zh: 一間擁有無窮多個房間的旅館已經全部客滿，但此時又來了一位新房客。

cues.en: The manager simply moves each guest from room n to room n plus one.
cues.zh: 經理只需要讓每位房客從第 n 號房搬到第 n+1 號房即可騰出空位。

cues.en: Infinity does not behave like ordinary finite numbers in daily arithmetic.
cues.zh: 無窮大的數學特性完全不同於日常生活中的普通有限數字。

oqGuJhOeMek.title: How Does Your Immune System Fight Viruses?

cues.en: Your body is a fortress protected by billions of microscopic soldiers.
cues.zh: 你的身體是一座由數十億微觀衛兵嚴密守護的鋼鐵堡壘。

cues.en: Macrophages engulf and digest foreign intruders on the biological front line.
cues.zh: 巨噬細胞在生物前線上負責吞噬並消化外來入侵者。

cues.en: Helper T cells coordinate complex biochemical counterattacks against active infections.
cues.zh: 輔助型 T 細胞負責統籌精密的生物化學反擊，撲滅活躍感染。

cues.en: Glass is solid and strong, yet light passes straight through it without obstacle.
cues.zh: 玻璃既堅固又結實，然而光線卻能毫無阻礙地穿透過去。

cues.en: Electrons in glass require more energy than visible light photons can provide.
cues.zh: 玻璃中的電子所躍遷需要的能量，高於可見光光子所能提供的量。

cues.en: Because photons cannot be absorbed, they continue traveling directly forward.
cues.zh: 因為光子無法被吸收，它們便直接穿過原子向前繼續行進。

vIdStMTgNl0.title: Can You Solve the Prisoner Box Riddle?

cues.en: One hundred prisoners must each find their own number among one hundred closed boxes.
cues.zh: 一百名囚犯必須各自在一頭密封的一百個盒子中找到自己的號碼。

cues.en: Independent random guessing yields a success probability of nearly zero.
cues.zh: 若各自獨立隨機猜測，全員成功的機率幾乎接近於零。

cues.en: Following closed loop cycles dramatically boosts the group survival odds.
cues.zh: 但遵循封閉循環路徑的策略，能奇蹟般將全體生還機率大幅提高。

zGoBFU1q4g0.title: What Causes Cavities and Tooth Decay?

cues.en: Trillions of bacteria live naturally on your teeth in a sticky film called plaque.
cues.zh: 數以兆計的細菌自然生活在牙齒表面稱為牙菌斑的黏性薄膜中。

cues.en: When you consume sugary foods, bacteria feast and produce corrosive acids.
cues.zh: 當你食用含糖食物時，細菌大快朵頤並分泌具有腐蝕性的酸類。

cues.en: Over time, this acid dissolves protective minerals in the hard tooth enamel.
cues.zh: 日積月累下，這些酸會溶解牙齒最堅硬外層琺瑯質中的保護性礦物質。

cues.en: Scientists have debated the evolutionary purpose of zebra stripes for over a century.
cues.zh: 一個多世紀以來，科學家們一直在爭論斑馬條紋的演化目的。

cues.en: Recent experiments indicate that stripes confuse the compound eyes of biting flies.
cues.zh: 近期的實驗表明，黑白相間的斑紋能干擾吸血叮咬蠅類的複眼視覺。

cues.en: Striped patterns disrupt the insect landing mechanism, preventing painful bites.
cues.zh: 條紋圖樣會擾亂昆蟲的著陸減速機制，保護斑馬免受疼痛叮咬。

7m8QlSPP7t0.title: How Tall Can Animals Grow on Earth?

cues.en: Physics imposes strict biomechanical limits on how large animals can become.
cues.zh: 物理學對動物在陸地上所能長到的最大體型設定了嚴格的力學限制。

cues.en: As an animal doubles in height, its weight multiplies by a factor of eight.
cues.zh: 當動物的身高翻倍時，其體重會以八倍的立方速率驚人暴增。

cues.en: Pumping blood up a thirty-foot neck requires immense cardiovascular pressures.
cues.zh: 將血液向上輸送至三十英尺高的長頸，需要極為強大的心血管血壓。

cues.en: Bread making is one of humanity's earliest and most delicious biotechnology experiments.
cues.zh: 製作麵包是人類最早且最美味的生物技術實驗之一。

cues.en: Yeast consumes sugars and releases carbon dioxide gas, causing dough to rise.
cues.zh: 酵母菌消耗糖分並釋放二氧化碳氣體，促使麵團蓬鬆膨起。

cues.en: Gluten proteins form an elastic network that traps gas bubbles inside.
cues.zh: 麵筋蛋白質形成一個具備彈性的網狀結構，將氣泡牢牢鎖在內部。

N5vJSNXPEwA.title: Can You Solve the Alien Abduction Riddle?

cues.en: You and your crew have been captured by mischievous alien researchers.
cues.zh: 你和你的組員被一群愛惡作劇的外星研究員抓上了太空飛船。

cues.en: Only one secret combination of switches will deactivate the particle beam.
cues.zh: 只有一組特定開關密碼組合能關閉困住你們的粒子力場光束。

cues.en: Logical deduction is your only tool to guarantee a safe return home.
cues.zh: 嚴謹的邏輯演繹推理是保證所有人安全回家的唯一工具。

yRwoReHd7XU.title: Why Is Blue So Rare in Nature?

cues.en: Almost all colors in animals come from pigments in their food or skin.
cues.zh: 動物身上幾乎所有的顏色都來自其食物或皮膚中的色素沈積。

cues.en: However, true blue chemical pigments are extraordinarily rare in vertebrate biology.
cues.zh: 然而，真正的藍色化學色素在脊椎動物生物學中極其罕見。

cues.en: Instead, blue animals use microscopic nanostructures that bend light wavelengths.
cues.zh: 相反地，藍色生物運用奈米級微觀結構折射光線波長，形成結構色。

Lm5cno_hijw.title: Why Are the Oscars So Prestigious?

cues.en: The Academy Awards began in 1929 as a private banquet for 270 guests.
cues.zh: 奧斯卡金像獎始於1929年，最初只是270位嘉賓的私人宴會。

cues.en: Over nearly a century, it evolved into the world's most watched cultural ceremony.
cues.zh: 歷經近一世紀，它演變為全球收視率最高的年度文化盛典。

cues.en: Winning an Oscar permanently elevates a filmmaker's prestige and box office potential.
cues.zh: 贏得奧斯卡獎能永久提升電影人的崇高威望與未來票房潛力。

U54n1lifzms.title: How Film Scores Emotionally Manipulate Us

cues.en: A single musical chord can transform a peaceful scene into pure terror.
cues.zh: 單單一個音樂和弦，就能將平靜祥和的畫面轉化為徹頭徹尾的恐怖。

cues.en: Composers use leitmotifs to associate specific melodies with beloved characters.
cues.zh: 作曲家運用主導動機，將特定旋律與心愛角色緊密連結。

cues.en: Music speaks directly to our subconscious before our rational brain catches up.
cues.zh: 在我們的理性大腦反應過來之前，音樂早已直擊潛意識。

uEuan077dxU.title: The Enigma of the Mona Lisa

cues.en: Millions travel to the Louvre each year to gaze upon a modest wooden panel.
cues.zh: 每年有數百萬人湧入羅浮宮，只為一睹一塊質樸木板上的畫作。

cues.en: Leonardo da Vinci applied dozens of translucent glaze layers called sfumato.
cues.zh: 李奧納多·達文西塗抹了數十道半透明色釉，這被稱為暈塗法。

cues.en: Her elusive expression seems to change depending on where your eyes focus.
cues.zh: 她那神秘莫測的微笑神情，似乎會隨著你視線聚焦的位置而悄然變化。

Y34eshkxE5o.title: How Pixar Crafts Perfect Emotional Stories

cues.en: Pixar films resonate across generations because they explore universal human vulnerabilities.
cues.zh: 皮克斯電影之所以能跨世代引發共鳴，是因為它們深刻探討了人類共通的脆弱。

cues.en: Every great protagonist must experience their foundational belief being challenged.
cues.zh: 每位出色的主角都必須經歷其根深蒂固的核心信念遭到徹底顛覆。

mLUwwNh9aEI.title: The Secrets of Broadway Musical Theater

cues.en: Broadway is the international pinnacle of live theatrical performance.
cues.zh: 百老匯是全球現場戲劇表演藝術的最高殿堂。

cues.en: Actors perform eight physically demanding shows every single week.
cues.zh: 演員們每週要完成八場對體力與聲音技巧要求極高的高難度演出。

cues.en: Gothic architecture aimed to create heaven on earth through soaring vertical height.
cues.zh: 哥德式建築致力於透過直衝雲霄的垂直高度，在人間營造出天堂殿堂。

cues.en: Flying buttresses redirected tremendous roof weight away from fragile stone walls.
cues.zh: 飛扶壁將屋頂沈重的巨大下壓力引導轉移，遠離了脆弱的石砌牆面。

RLw8_5nUxQ4.title: Why Vincent van Gogh Cut Off His Ear

cues.en: Vincent van Gogh sold only a handful of paintings during his turbulent lifetime.
cues.zh: 文森·梵谷在他動盪不安的一生中，僅僅售出了屈指可數的幾幅畫作。

cues.en: His vivid colors and swirling brushstrokes expressed raw, unadulterated passion.
cues.zh: 他那明亮強烈的色彩與筆觸，抒發了最純粹無瑕的情感。

a9WprkKesKI.title: The Evolution of Video Game Music

cues.en: Early game composers worked within strict limitations of just three audio channels.
cues.zh: 早期的遊戲作曲家必須在僅有三個音頻通道的極嚴苛限制下創作。

cues.en: Memorable melodies had to be catchy enough to loop endlessly without annoying players.
cues.zh: 好記的旋律必須足夠悅耳，才能無休止循環播放而不令玩家煩躁。

GkWzOJaAYS0.title: How Film Noir Defined Modern Cinema

cues.en: Film noir emerged in the nineteen-forties reflecting post-war cynicism and moral ambiguity.
cues.zh: 黑色電影興起於1940年代，反映出戰後社會的犬儒心態與道德模糊性。

cues.en: High-contrast lighting created deep, expressive shadows across rain-soaked streets.
cues.zh: 高對比度的明暗佈光在街道上投射出幽深且具表現力的陰影。

8HGjm0Sk8tk.title: The Genius of Studio Ghibli's Background Art

cues.en: Studio Ghibli landscapes evoke a profound sense of nostalgia and quiet contemplation.
cues.zh: 吉卜力工作室的風景畫面喚起了一種深沉的懷舊感與靜謐的沉思。

cues.en: Artists use traditional poster color paints to render rich, tactile natural environments.
cues.zh: 美術師運用手繪廣告顏料技法，描繪出層次豐富的自然環境。

_RxBjsyJcuE.title: How Michelangelo Painted the Sistine Chapel

cues.en: Michelangelo considered himself a sculptor, yet was tasked with painting twelve thousand square feet.
cues.zh: 米開朗基羅自視為一名雕刻家，卻被委託繪製一萬兩千平方英尺的巨大天頂。

cues.en: He stood for four grueling years on custom wooden scaffolding applying wet plaster fresco.
cues.zh: 他在木製鷹架上艱苦仰立了整整四年，日復一日塗抹濕壁畫灰漿。

ofk-aw5G-FQ.title: Why Comic Books Are Serious Literature

cues.en: Graphic novels combine visual art with sophisticated narrative prose.
cues.zh: 圖像小說巧妙地將視覺藝術與高水準的文學敘事散文融為一體。

cues.en: The space between panels invites readers to actively participate in the pacing.
cues.zh: 畫格與畫格之間的留白，邀請讀者主動參與到故事節奏的想像中。

sfAyXjRFUJk.title: Why the Global Semiconductor Chip Shortage Happened

cues.en: Modern society runs entirely on tiny silicone wafers packed with billions of transistors.
cues.zh: 現代社會完全運轉在裝載了數十億電晶體的微小矽晶圓之上。

cues.en: Taiwan manufactures over sixty percent of the world's most advanced microchips.
cues.zh: 台灣製造了全球超過百分之六十的最尖端先進晶片。

xi6r3hZe5Tg.title: Renewable Energy Transition: Progress and Challenges

cues.en: Solar and wind energy have plummeted in cost, becoming cheaper than fossil fuels.
cues.zh: 太陽能與風力發電的成本大幅暴跌，已變得比化石燃料更加便宜。

cues.en: The critical hurdle is battery storage capacity when the sun is not shining.
cues.zh: 當前最關鍵的瓶頸在於無日照或無風時的超大型電池儲能容量。

tNla9nyRMmQ.title: Why Are Housing Prices So High Worldwide?

cues.en: In major metropolitan centers, home prices have dramatically outpaced median wage growth.
cues.zh: 在各大國際都會中心，房價漲幅已大幅超越了實質中位數工資的增長。

cues.en: Increasing housing supply remains the single most effective policy to restore affordability.
cues.zh: 大幅增加住宅市場供給量，依然是恢復一般人負擔能力的唯一最有效良方。

RDFBbxMDi1U.title: The War on Plastic Waste: Where Does It Actually Go?

cues.en: Less than ten percent of all plastic produced has ever been successfully recycled.
cues.zh: 人類歷史上生產的所有塑膠製品中，成功被回收利用的比例不到百分之十。

cues.en: Single-use plastics often end up in landfills or wash into oceanic gyres.
cues.zh: 大量一次性塑膠最終落入垃圾掩埋場，或被沖入浩瀚的遠洋環流當中。

t-8TDOFqkQA.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Jobs

cues.en: Generative AI is shifting automation from physical labor to creative and intellectual tasks.
cues.zh: 生成式人工智慧正在將自動化浪潮從體力勞動擴展至創意與腦力工作。

cues.en: Jobs that require deep empathy, strategic judgment, and human connection will endure.
cues.zh: 那些需要深厚同理心、宏觀戰略判斷與真實人際連結的工作將歷久不衰。

3ayZ70mGhw8.title: Space Tourism: The Billionaire Race to Orbit

cues.en: Commercial spaceflight is transitioning from science fiction into an accessible luxury market.
cues.zh: 商業太空飛行正在從科幻小說情節轉化為富豪可觸及的高端奢華市場。

cues.en: Reusable rockets have lowered the cost per kilogram of launching into Earth orbit.
cues.zh: 可重複使用火箭技術極大幅度地降低了將每公斤物體送入地球軌道的成本。

Y02j-VOdnO0.title: Why Are Bees Dying at Alarming Rates?

cues.en: Honeybees pollinate one-third of the food crops that sustain human populations.
cues.zh: 蜜蜂負責為供養全人類生存所需的三分之一糧食作物進行關鍵授粉。

cues.en: Protecting native pollinators is directly linked to global food security.
cues.zh: 保護本土授粉昆蟲直接關乎整個地球未來的糧食安全與物價穩定。

C65iqOSCZOY.title: The Global Water Crisis: Running Out of Freshwater

cues.en: Freshwater accounts for less than three percent of all water on planet Earth.
cues.zh: 在整個地球所有的水資源中，淡水所佔的比例不到百分之三。

cues.en: Ancient underground aquifers are being depleted much faster than rainfall can replenish them.
cues.zh: 古老的地下深層蓄水層正在以遠快於雨水自然補給的速度被過度抽乾。

oZ4Lj_AVk44.title: Cybersecurity Threats in the Cloud Era

cues.en: Cyberattacks on hospitals and power grids demonstrate that digital wars have real-world consequences.
cues.zh: 對醫院和電網的網路攻擊表明，數位戰場的破壞會帶來真實世界的嚴重災難。

cues.en: Multi-factor authentication remains the single most effective defense against credential theft.
cues.zh: 多重身分驗證仍然是抵禦密碼憑證失竊最簡單有效的防線。

rkxMdmipYqM.title: The Rise of Electric Vehicles Worldwide

cues.en: Electric vehicles are transforming automobile manufacturing from mechanical engineering to software development.
cues.zh: 電動車正在將汽車製造業從傳統機械工程徹底轉變為軟體與電池主導。

cues.en: Widespread fast-charging infrastructure is key to mass consumer adoption.
cues.zh: 廣泛普及的超快充基礎設施是推動大眾消費者全面採購電動車的關鍵所在。

00NIQgQE_d4.title: Why Fast Fashion Is an Environmental Disaster

cues.en: Fast fashion brands release dozens of new micro-seasons every year at throwaway prices.
cues.zh: 快時尚品牌每年以極其低廉的拋棄式價格推出數十個微型新品季節。

cues.en: Millions of tons of synthetic garments end up in the Atacama Desert or open incinerators.
cues.zh: 數百萬噸合成纖維廢棄衣物最終堆積在沙漠或露天焚化爐中。

7vSMcb9X3kU.title: The Global Microplastic Crisis Inside Human Bodies

cues.en: Microplastics have now been detected in human bloodstreams, lungs, and newborn placenta tissue.
cues.zh: 微塑膠顆粒如今已在人體血液、肺部以及新生兒胎盤組織中被陸續檢測出來。

cues.en: Medical researchers are investigating the long-term cellular inflammatory responses.
cues.zh: 醫學研究人員正在深入調查微塑膠引發的長期細胞慢性發炎反應。

cues.en: The World Trade Organization establishes binding ground rules for international commerce.
cues.zh: 世界貿易組織為國際商業貿易活動確立了具備約束力的基本規則。

cues.en: Its dispute settlement mechanism aims to resolve tariff disagreements peacefully through arbitration.
cues.zh: 其爭端解決機制旨在透過中立仲裁，和平化解各國之間的關稅分歧。

yd1JhZzoS6A.title: How the Internet Submarine Cables Connect Continents

cues.en: Ninety-nine percent of international internet traffic travels through underwater fiber optic cables.
cues.zh: 全球百分之九十九的國際網路數據流量，都是經由水下海底光纖電纜傳輸的。

cues.en: Armored shielding protects cables from anchor drag, underwater earthquakes, and shark bites.
cues.zh: 厚重的鋼甲防護層保護電纜免受船錨拖拽、海底地震以及鯊魚啃咬的損壞。

qD1pnquN_DM.title: Learn Daily Morning Routine in English

cues.en: Good morning! Time to wake up and start a wonderful new day.
cues.zh: 早安！該起床迎接美好嶄新的一天了。

cues.en: First, I wash my face and brush my teeth thoroughly.
cues.zh: 首先，我把臉洗乾淨，並認真仔細地刷牙。

cues.en: Then, I put on my favorite clean clothes for school.
cues.zh: 接著，我穿上最心愛的乾淨衣服準備上學。

cues.en: Breakfast is ready! Fresh milk, warm eggs, and crispy toast.
cues.zh: 早餐準備好了！有新鮮牛奶、熱呼呼的雞蛋和香脆吐司。

YRonvWl1g1s.title: Colors of the Rainbow and Everyday Objects

cues.en: Red is the color of a ripe, juicy apple.
cues.zh: 紅色是一顆熟透多汁的大蘋果。

cues.en: Yellow is the warm sunshine high in the sky.
cues.zh: 黃色是高高掛在天空中的溫暖陽光。

cues.en: Green is the soft grass beneath our joyful feet.
cues.zh: 綠色是我們腳下柔軟翠綠的青青草地。

zXEq-QO3xTg.title: Meet the Farm Animals and Their Sounds

cues.en: Old MacDonald had a farm, and on that farm he had a cow.
cues.zh: 老麥克唐納有一個大農場，農場裡養了一頭乳牛。

cues.en: The cow says 'Moo, moo' all day long in the meadow.
cues.zh: 乳牛在草地上整天開心地哞哞叫。

cues.en: The little sheep says 'Baa, baa' with its fluffy white wool.
cues.zh: 披著毛茸茸白毛的小綿羊則是咩咩叫個不停。

Aq4UAss33qA.title: Counting Numbers from 1 to 20 with Fun

cues.en: One, two, three, four, five! Count the little fingers on your hand.
cues.zh: 一、二、三、四、五！數數你小手上的手指頭。

cues.en: Six, seven, eight, nine, ten! Now let's count them all again.
cues.zh: 六、七、八、九、十！現在讓我們一起再來數一遍。

cues.en: Bananas are sweet and yellow, full of energy and potassium.
cues.zh: 香蕉香甜又金黃，富含飽滿能量與鉀元素。

cues.en: Carrots are crunchy and orange, helping your eyes see bright and clear.
cues.zh: 胡蘿蔔清脆又鮮橙，能幫助你的雙眼明亮清澈。

RuqvGiZi0qg.title: Parts of the Body Song: Head, Shoulders, Knees

cues.en: Head, shoulders, knees, and toes, knees and toes!
cues.zh: 頭兒、肩膀、膝蓋、腳趾頭，膝蓋與腳趾頭！

cues.en: Eyes, and ears, and mouth, and nose!
cues.zh: 眼睛、耳朵、嘴巴、還有小鼻子！

5cYMu3RTMJU.title: Days of the Week and Months of the Year

cues.en: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday!
cues.zh: 星期一、星期二、星期三、星期四、星期五、星期六、星期天！

cues.en: Seven days are in a week, let's sing them loud and proud.
cues.zh: 一個星期有七天，讓我們大聲自豪地唱出來。

BdrZWu2dZ4c.title: Vehicles on the Go: Car, Train, Airplane, Boat

cues.en: The red car drives 'Vroom, vroom' along the winding street.
cues.zh: 紅色小汽車在蜿蜒的街道上轟轟奔馳。

cues.en: The big steam train goes 'Choo, choo' on the steel tracks.
cues.zh: 巨大的蒸汽火車在鐵軌上發出鏘鏘的汽笛聲。

GR2o6k8aPlI.title: My Family: Mommy, Daddy, Brother, Sister

cues.en: This is my mommy, kind and sweet, she bakes the best cookies.
cues.zh: 這是我溫柔親切的媽媽，她烤的餅乾最好吃了。

cues.en: This is my daddy, tall and strong, he reads me bedtime stories.
cues.zh: 這是我高大強壯的爸爸，他每晚為我讀睡前故事。

o5jZIswSfSE.title: Feelings and Emotions: Happy, Sad, Angry, Excited

cues.en: When I get a big ice cream cone, I feel super happy!
cues.zh: 當我拿到一支大冰淇淋甜筒時，我覺得超級開心！

cues.en: When my toy breaks, I feel sad, but a hug makes it better.
cues.zh: 當心愛玩具摔壞時我會難過，但一個溫暖擁抱就能讓我好過些。

P9abGg_gF1s.title: Weather Words: Sunny, Rainy, Windy, Snowy

cues.en: How is the weather today? Look outside the window!
cues.zh: 今天的天氣如何呢？快轉頭看看窗外吧！

cues.en: It is sunny! Put on your sun hat and let's play outside.
cues.zh: 今天是個大晴天！戴上遮陽帽，我們去戶外玩耍吧。

LF3crlV28xA.title: Opposites Song: Big & Small, Fast & Slow

cues.en: An elephant is big, and a little mouse is small.
cues.zh: 大象的體型無比巨大，而小老鼠非常嬌小。

cues.en: The cheetah runs fast, but the sleepy turtle crawls slow.
cues.zh: 獵豹奔跑如飛，但慢吞吞的烏龜爬行得非常緩慢。

SFE0mMWbA-Y.title: Clean Up Song: Putting Toys Away Together

cues.en: Clean up, clean up, everybody everywhere!
cues.zh: 收拾乾淨、收拾乾淨，大家隨時隨地動手整理！

cues.en: Clean up, clean up, everybody do your share!
cues.zh: 收拾乾淨、收拾乾淨，每個人都盡自己的一份力量！

yCjJyiqpAuU.title: Bedtime Lullaby: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star

cues.en: Twinkle, twinkle, little star, how I wonder what you are!
cues.zh: 一閃一閃小星星，我多麼好奇你究竟是什麼！

cues.en: Up above the world so high, like a diamond in the sky.
cues.zh: 高高掛在整個世界之上，宛如夜空中璀璨閃爍的鑽石。

oWCgGPVMkwA.title: How to Pack a Carry-on Bag for 2 Weeks of Travel

cues.en: Traveling light gives you total mobility and peace of mind on the road.
cues.zh: 輕裝旅行能給你在旅途中帶來無拘無束的行動自由與安心感。

cues.en: Choose merino wool garments that naturally resist odors over multiple days.
cues.zh: 挑選美麗諾羊毛衣物，能在多日穿著下依然自然透氣抗異味。

cues.en: Rolling your clothes compresses fabrics while preventing stubborn wrinkles.
cues.zh: 用捲衣方式收納衣物能緊密壓縮布料，同時有效避免頑固折痕。

-dxy510zGj8.title: Tokyo Hidden Gems: Beyond the Tourist Crowds

cues.en: Tokyo's true soul lives in the quiet residential alleys tucked behind neon skyscrapers.
cues.zh: 東京真正的靈魂棲息在霓虹摩天大樓背後靜謐淳樸的住宅小巷之中。

cues.en: Traditional kissaten coffee shops serve hand-drip brew with retro nostalgic jazz.
cues.zh: 傳統懷舊喫茶店伴隨著復古爵士樂，為客人端上一杯杯手沖咖啡。

xgFInCmXrPw.title: How to Order Coffee Like a Local in Italy

cues.en: In Italy, drinking coffee at the counter is a sacred daily social ritual.
cues.zh: 在義大利，站在吧台旁喝杯咖啡是每天不可或缺的神聖社交儀式。

cues.en: Ordering 'un caffe' gets you a rich, dark espresso with golden crema.
cues.zh: 點一杯 'un caffè'，咖啡師就會為你遞上一杯覆滿金黃油沫的濃縮咖啡。

9BZk6eVMa00.title: How to Plan a Budget European Backpacking Trip

cues.en: Traveling Europe on a budget is about prioritizing experiences over luxury consumption.
cues.zh: 小資遊歷歐洲的核心關鍵在於將豐富體驗置於昂貴奢華消費之上。

cues.en: Staying in hostels allows you to make lifelong friends with adventurous travelers worldwide.
cues.zh: 入住青年旅館能讓你有機會與來自世界各地熱愛冒險的旅人結為摯友。

kYXiegTXsEs.title: Solo Travel: How to Embrace Being on Your Own

cues.en: Traveling solo forces you out of your comfort zone and into deep self-discovery.
cues.zh: 獨自一人旅行會迫使你跨出熟悉的舒適圈，進入深刻的自我探索之中。

cues.en: When you have nobody else to rely on, your resilience and confidence flourish.
cues.zh: 當身邊沒有任何人可以依賴時，你的適應韌性與內在自信便會蓬勃綻放。

MY3Qy6vAbZQ.title: Street Food Tour in Bangkok, Thailand

cues.en: Bangkok is universally celebrated as the street food capital of Southeast Asia.
cues.zh: 曼谷被舉世公認為整個東南亞無可爭議的街頭美食之都。

cues.en: Wok hei is the smoky, intense flavor achieved by cooking over fiery charcoal heat.
cues.zh: 「鑊氣」是在熊熊木炭烈火高溫快炒下所迸發出的獨特濃郁焦香風味。

7glld8yO3Xo.title: The Art of Slow Living in the Countryside

cues.en: Modern cities accelerate our internal clocks to an unsustainable, frantic tempo.
cues.zh: 現代都市將我們內在的心靈時鐘加速到了一種難以承受的狂躁節奏。

cues.en: Reconnecting with the natural rhythm of plants restores our psychological equilibrium.
cues.zh: 重新融入大自然花草樹木的生長律動，能逐步修復我們失衡的心理天秤。

L4lo55OA4WY.title: Scuba Diving the Great Barrier Reef

cues.en: The Great Barrier Reef is so vast that it can be clearly seen from outer space.
cues.zh: 澳洲大堡礁的規模無比浩瀚，甚至從外太空都能清晰俯瞰到它的輪廓。

cues.en: Coral reefs shelter a quarter of all marine species despite covering tiny ocean floor area.
cues.zh: 珊瑚礁儘管僅佔海床極小面積，卻庇護了全球整整四分之一的海洋生物物種。

cues.en: Classical computers store information in bits that exist as either a zero or a one.
cues.zh: 傳統電腦將資訊儲存在僅能非零即一的傳統位元之中。

cues.en: Quantum qubits leverage superposition to calculate multiple probabilities simultaneously.
cues.zh: 量子電腦的量子位元（Qubit）利用疊加態同時並行運算多種機率可能。

cues.en: This revolutionary paradigm could revolutionize drug discovery and climate modeling.
cues.zh: 這種革命性的計算典範有望徹底重塑新藥研發與複雜氣候模擬預測。

mZsaaturR6E.title: Nuclear Fusion: Recreating the Sun on Earth

cues.en: Nuclear fusion powers the stars by smashing hydrogen isotopes together under extreme gravity.
cues.zh: 核融合透過在極端引力下撞擊聚合氫同位素，為整座宇宙繁星提供源源不絕的能量。

cues.en: Unlike fission, fusion produces zero long-lived radioactive waste and cannot melt down.
cues.zh: 與核分裂截然不同，核融合不產生長半衰期放射性核廢料，且完全無熔毀風險。

6tw_JVz_IEc.title: CRISPR Gene Editing: Rewriting the Code of Life

cues.en: CRISPR-Cas9 functions like molecular scissors that can precisely cut and edit DNA.
cues.zh: CRISPR-Cas9 宛如微觀的分子剪刀，能以分子級精度精確剪輯修改 DNA。

cues.en: Scientists can now correct faulty genetic mutations that cause debilitating inherited diseases.
cues.zh: 科學家如今有能力精準矯正導致頑固遺傳性罕見疾病的缺陷基因突變。

uSMGENDH_QI.title: James Webb Space Telescope: Peering into Cosmic Dawn

cues.en: The James Webb Space Telescope orbits one million miles away from Earth.
cues.zh: 詹姆斯·韋伯太空望遠鏡運轉在距離地球一百萬英里外的日地拉格朗日點。

cues.en: Its gold-coated mirrors capture faint infrared light emitted shortly after the Big Bang.
cues.zh: 其鍍金主反射鏡能精準捕捉大爆炸後不久所散發出的微弱古老紅外光。

cues.en: Artificial neural networks are inspired by the interconnected structure of biological brains.
cues.zh: 人工類神經網路的構想靈感源自生物大腦神經元之間相互緊密連接的網絡結構。

cues.en: Gradient descent iteratively adjusts millions of weights to minimize classification error.
cues.zh: 梯度下降演算法藉由反覆微調數百萬個權重參數，以將模型預測誤差最小化。

62SmQuMNE0w.title: Bionic Prosthetics: Merging Humans and Machines

cues.en: Targeted muscle reinnervation allows severed nerves to communicate directly with robotic limbs.
cues.zh: 神經再分佈手術使截肢殘留神經能直接向精密的機器人義肢發送大腦運動指令。

cues.en: Sensors on prosthetic fingertips send electrical pulses back to the patient's brain.
cues.zh: 義肢指尖裝載的微型感測器能將壓力電脈衝傳回大腦，重建真實觸覺反饋。

9OVtk6G2TnQ.title: Why Solid-State Batteries Will Change Everything

cues.en: Solid-state batteries replace flammable liquid electrolytes with solid ceramic compounds.
cues.zh: 固態電池使用固態陶瓷化合物取代了傳統鋰離子電池中易燃的液態電解質。

cues.en: They offer twice the energy density while practically eliminating the risk of fire.
cues.zh: 它們能提供兩倍以上的驚人能量密度，同時從物理根源上消除了自燃起火風險。

iHzzSao6ypE.title: How Autonomous Self-Driving Cars See the World

cues.en: LiDAR pulses millions of laser beams per second to create a 3D digital map.
cues.zh: 光達系統每秒發射數百萬道雷射光束，在車身周圍構建出高精度的3D數位空間點雲地圖。

cues.en: Sensor fusion combines cameras, radar, and laser data to predict pedestrian movement.
cues.zh: 多感測器融合演算法綜合攝影機、雷達與雷射數據，精準預測行人的下一個動向。

cues.en: Fasting lowers insulin levels and allows the body to access stored adipose fuel.
